mode.name: structural
mode.desc: a juncture or boundary; belongs to no segment's feature bag

mode.name: prosodic
mode.desc: belongs to the unit, not to its feature bag

mode.name: release
mode.desc: names a phase of the segment, never the whole of it

mode.name: approach
mode.desc: names the phase a segment is entered on; stated by a mark written before the base

mode.name: secondary
mode.desc: a secondary articulation: adds a constriction, keeps the primary

mode.name: additive
mode.desc: adds only what the base leaves unstated

feature.name: channel
feature.desc: Where the airflow channel sits in cross-section: the mid-sagittal plane projects this axis away, so it has no contour, only an ordering

feature.name: articulator
feature.desc: Active articulator: the organ that moves to make the constriction, ordered by its home position along the tract

feature.name: tie
feature.desc: Tie bar sense: binds constituents into one unit

feature.name: linking
feature.desc: Linking (absence of a break) between words

feature.name: approach
feature.desc: The phase a stop closure is entered on

feature.name: tone
feature.desc: Pitch, as a sequence of levels in time order

feature.name: contour
feature.desc: Pitch shape: the move between each adjacent pair of levels

bridge.name: laterality
bridge.desc: Airflow at the sides of the tongue

projection.desc: Glottal state, read two ways instead of four

notation.name: extension
notation.desc: A convention outside the IPA chart

symbol.desc: the chart has no symbol for silence
generative phonology; the IPA marks groups with '|' and '‖'
set theory; the structural zero declared below
